title: A conserved mechanism for dimerization and activation of superfamily 1A UvrD-family helicases.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran the paper context tool: data availability statement reads 'shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author'; no accession numbers of their own in the text. Downloaded and unzipped the whole Europe PMC supplement (0.6 MB, 15 files): 7 figure images in two formats each, one scheme image, and one 24 KB PDF of supplementary figures plus a table of DNA oligonucleotide sequences. No numeric data file of any kind (no csv, tsv, xlsx). Queried the only deposited structure the text mentions, PDB (Protein Data Bank) entry 9DES, via the RCSB application programming interface: it is a 7 Angstrom cryo-electron microscopy map (EMDB EMD-46797) belonging to this group's earlier 2025 PNAS paper, not to this one.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the measurements are ensemble stopped-flow and single-molecule fluorescence unwinding/translocation experiments on a handful of engineered helicase constructs (Rep A416C, UvrD R421C, PcrA S425C, plus cysteine-free parents), and the reported rate and processivity values, which appear only inside figures and prose. Buffer conditions and oligonucleotide designs came from the methods section.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. The data availability statement says the underlying data 'will be shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author' — the checklist's explicit A1 fail condition. I opened the entire supplement and it contains only figure images and an oligonucleotide sequence table; no measurement file exists to download. The one structure accession in the text (PDB 9DES) is from the authors' previous 2025 paper.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL (not reached, but obvious). Any label — unwinding rate, processivity, dimerization affinity — exists only as numbers printed in figure panels and prose; it would have to be hand-transcribed or read off plots, i.e. constructed rather than read from a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed in files. Protein sequences are inferable (wild-type UvrD, Rep, PcrA, Mtb UvrD1 plus named point mutations) and DNA substrate sequences are listed in Supplementary Table S1, so inputs would be obtainable — but there are only a few of them.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed in files. The methods and figure axes do state units (per second, base pairs, micromolar), so units would not be the problem here.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The experimental unit is a protein construct under a redox condition: roughly four helicases times a handful of variants and conditions, i.e. tens of measurements at most, versus the ~1,500-row minimum. I could not count rows because no table exists.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small — the entire supplement is 0.6 MB, mostly images. Size was never the issue.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no downloadable table, so no count to reconcile against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle — rates and processivities are direct biophysical measurements (stopped-flow fluorescence, single-molecule traces), not another model's output. But they are not released.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural backbone for helicase sequence or variant-effect work
backbone.hardware: CPU-only laptop would suffice for embeddings of a few protein sequences, but there are far too few labelled examples to fit any head
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; irrelevant here because no training data is available

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. UniProt (protein sequence and annotation) and AlphaFold DB (predicted structures) would join on UniProt accession for UvrD, Rep, PcrA and Mtb UvrD1, but joining four proteins to a large resource adds no labels.
integration.join_key: UniProt accession (would have to be assigned by hand; not present in any file)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with measurements on roughly four helicases there is no quantity a joined resource could help predict.

controls.positive_control: Not applicable — no dataset to run controls on.
controls.external_validation: The group's own earlier Mycobacterium tuberculosis UvrD1 work (PNAS 2025, PDB 9DES / EMDB EMD-46797) is the closest independent source, but it is structural, not a labelled measurement set.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no quantitative data, so there is nothing a model could be trained on or evaluated against.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use helicase protein sequence and mutation identity to predict how fast and how far the enzyme unwinds DNA.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need: the protein sequence of each helicase variant plus its DNA substrate and redox condition. Verified count available: zero rows, because no measurement table is published.
plain_idea.predict: Unwinding rate (base pairs per second) and processivity (base pairs travelled before falling off), measured by stopped-flow fluorescence and single-molecule fluorescence experiments in this lab.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: In principle, structural biologists engineering constitutively active helicases would like to know which 2B-domain substitutions activate an enzyme without testing each one; in practice this paper supplies far too few measurements, and none in machine-readable form, to learn that.

ml_idea: The only idea the paper suggests — predict whether a cysteine substitution in the 2B regulatory domain converts a superfamily 1A helicase into a constitutively active covalent dimer, from sequence and structure — is a beautiful mechanistic result but a dataset of about four proteins. There is no viable machine-learning project here.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimated because there is no dataset; the only files are 0.6 MB of figure images and a 24 KB supplementary PDF, which I unzipped and inspected.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement, then unzip the supplement and look for any tabular file. Took one command and killed it: 'shared on reasonable request', and the supplement is images plus an oligonucleotide list.

verdict_reason: No data released — 'available on reasonable request' — and only tens of measurements exist anyway (A1 and A5 fail).
